ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, within the same Cartesian coordinate system, the graphs of the functions $y_1=|x|$ and $y_2=kx+b$ intersect at points $A(-1, 1)$ and $B(2, 2)$. Based on the graph, what is the solution set of the inequality $|x|-kx-b\ge 0$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Observing the graph, we find: when $x\le -1$ or $x\ge 2$, the graph of the function $y_1=|x|$ is above or intersects with the graph of $y_2=kx+b$, \\
$\because |x|-kx-b\ge 0$, \\
$\therefore |x| \ge kx+b$, \\
$\therefore$ the solution set of the inequality $|x|-kx-b\ge 0$ is $x\le -1$ or $x\ge 2$. \\
Thus, the answer is: $\boxed{x\le -1$ or $x\ge 2}$
